lesson_title: The One Page Banks Read First
hook_text: A bank manager spends about two minutes on your business plan. Which page decides your loan?
clip_script: You want to start a mobile car wash. You need R15 000 and a bank loan. The bank manager opens your business plan. The first page after the contents is the executive summary: the whole plan on one page. What you sell, who buys, how much you need, how you will repay. It is placed first, but you write it last, because it sums up everything else. Behind it: the business description with your vision, mission and SMART goals. The product. The market and a SWOT. The marketing, production, management and financial plans. The appendices with quotes and survey results. And one rule above all: the numbers must match. If the price is R120 on page five, it is R120 on page twelve. Plan first, then drive.
visual_style: A busy bank desk with a stack of plans, one plan opened to a clean one-page summary, then a fast flip through clearly labelled sections, ending on a matching R120 highlighted in two places.
pacing: A fast opening, a brisk flip through the sections, a firm closing rule.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and start your own business plan with a vision, mission and three SMART goals.
